judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.3 lists Project Manual date as none and Document/Title/Pages as 'TBD,' so the Specifications are never identified; A201 1.1.6 and 1.2.1 assume identified Specifications.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Drawings are 'dated [blank]' with the list left as 'TBD'; no drawings are identified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 1.1.5 and 3.11 presuppose identified Drawings, and Addendum 6.5/3.10.5 contemplate drawings developed later and made part of the Contract Documents; the enumeration gap is real but partly cured by the fast-track scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists the two addenda with page counts but leaves the Date column blank; the closing sentence about bidding requirements is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Article 1's list and with the Addendum/Supplementary Conditions themselves; the missing dates are minor since the documents are named.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Lists Exhibits A–E by title; Exhibit B has no page count and the entries are terse, but each exhibit is identifiable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The listed exhibits (C's 5% hand-tool markup, D's 1% insurance rate) add cost items that Article 7 does not expressly describe and 8.1.7 excludes; the enumeration incorporates provisions in tension with Articles 7 and 8.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The article heading is followed only by the bracketed instruction; no limits of liability or bond requirements are inserted, so the insurance article is empty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 11.1.2 requires insurance 'written for not less than limits of liability specified in the Contract Documents or required by law,' and Exhibit E is only a certificate; the absence of specified limits leaves a gap that A201 and the Supplementary Conditions 11.x must fill.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard execution recital, definite as to copies and distribution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature blocks and the Addendum/Supplementary Conditions execution blanks (day and month left blank) are incomplete, but that is an execution formality rather than an internal contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Recites incorporation and states the Agreement is 'dated February 1, 2002' for the purpose of modifying, supplementing and amending; definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement's own opening recites 'as of the First day of ... Two Thousand Two' with a garbled month, and the parties are 'Mr. & Mrs. Paul Stephens' — dating consistency is plausible but not verifiable; also the Addendum both attaches to and is enumerated in the Agreement it modifies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds duties framed by 'only skilled and properly trained staff' and 'one appropriately skilled and experienced supervisory employee' who may take other work only if it 'does not impair his or her ability' — those qualitative standards are the soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Overlaps A201 3.9's superintendent requirement and 3.4.3's skilled-worker duty; the designated 'person responsible for this project' and the superintendent may or may not be the same, which is unaddressed.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Pending approval of permits' is an unexplained condition attached to a fixed date; it is unclear whether commencement is postponed if permits are late.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Contract Time runs from commencement (4.2) and Substantial Completion is a fixed calendar date under Addendum 4.3, so a permit-driven slip in commencement does not shift the completion date — an unreconciled interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed calendar date subject to adjustments as provided; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Because commencement is 'pending approval of permits' (Addendum 4.1) while completion is a fixed date, and no liquidated damages provision was inserted in Agreement 4.3, the time scheme is only loosely integrated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bonus is 'a sum to be determined' and division is 'as determined by the Owner' — an unpriced, wholly discretionary obligation with no formula, so the promise is arguably illusory.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.3's bracket for bonus/liquidated damages was left blank, and A201 4.3.10 waives consequential damages; nothing else supplies the bonus measure, so the clause stands alone with no mechanism.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long fast-track pricing mechanism resting on 'industry-standard figures,' 'Contractor's current best estimate,' negotiation 'to the satisfaction of Owner' and Owner's 'sole and absolute discretion' to terminate — several open standards plus a one-sided termination right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It creates a Contract Sum refined by Change Order in a form built around a Guaranteed Maximum Price that is N/A, and its termination right is not among the termination grounds in Agreement 13 or A201 14; the Preliminary Budget also becomes a Contract Document affecting 12.1.5's schedule of values.
judgments.clause_name: First Addendum § 6.5 — Preliminary Budget and Schedule of Values

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Capable of being prevented through timely notice of an unsafe condition' is a vague counterfactual test, and 'anyone for whom either is responsible' broadens the exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It narrows 7.7.2's reimbursement while A201 10.6.1 gives the Contractor emergency discretion and entitles it to additional compensation determined under 4.3 and Article 7; the two entitlements pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a proviso turning on whether absence of collectible insurance is due to the Contractor's failure to maintain 'required insurance' or 'breach of a contract for insurance'; 'required insurance' is undefined here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 16 of the Agreement, which should state insurance limits, is blank, so what insurance was 'required' is uncertain; Supplementary Conditions 11.6 and A201 11.1.2 must be consulted.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of items covered by the Fee closing with 'and none of these items shall be subject to direct reimbursement under Article 7'; the items are specific but 'administrative support' and 'all main office overhead' are broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It bears the same number as the original 8.1.8 (GMP-exceeding costs) yet addresses a wholly different subject, so the original 8.1.8 is either deleted or displaced without saying which; that numbering collision is a genuine coherence problem alongside 7.2.2/7.2.3 site-versus-office allocations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite seven-day notice and funding-opportunity mechanism, though the consequence of non-compliance is left implicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Article 9.1's default allocation of discounts; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introductory phrase conditioning submissions on being 'in form and substance satisfactory to Owner and Architect' — a satisfaction standard, but standard in payment applications.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Duplicates the number 12.1.4 already used in the Agreement, and 12.1.7.5 cross-refers to 'the documentation required by Paragraph 12.1.4'; which 12.1.4 is meant is not stated.
judgments.clause_name: 12.1.4 [New] Items accompanying each Application for Payment

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed enumerated statement requirement; 'when appropriate, from lower tier subcontractors' is the only soft edge.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 9.6.3 and 9.3.1's requirement of subcontractor requisitions; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear $2,500 threshold and a defined document type; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 9.10.2's waiver-and-release regime and with Addendum 12.2.2's lien-free endorsement condition; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure catch-all — 'such other information, documentation, and material as Owner or the Architect reasonably may require' — appended to two enumerated specifics, leaving its reach uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Similar open language appears in Agreement 12.1.4 ('any other evidence required'); consistent in kind, so no distinct relational defect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Substitutes 5% retainage into an otherwise mechanical formula; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Replaces the 'N/A' figures in Agreement 12.1.7.3 and coexists with the 10% subcontractor retainage in 12.1.8, and still computes on Cost of the Work whose GMP context is absent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Adds a single definite precondition of duly published and recorded Notice of Completion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Addendum 12.2.2's recordation-based payment date and with A201 9.10; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two alternative deadlines with a 'whichever is earlier' rule; arithmetically clear, though tying final payment to a lien-free title endorsement makes timing partly dependent on a third party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces Agreement 12.2.2's 30-days-after-final-Certificate rule and is keyed to recordation rather than certification, while 12.2.3 still sets Architect certification deadlines; the sequencing across the two documents is awkward but reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson' names alternatives without stating whose act binds; 'or' leaves authority indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 2.1.1.1 says the authorized representative 'is Mary Williamson' and then lists three individuals who may act, which does not match this formulation; A201 2.1.1 requires a designated representative with express binding authority.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Introductory warranty clause with a clear survival provision; the parenthetical 'in addition to any other representations and warranties contained in the Contract Documents' is broad but ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Occupies the number 14.6 which in the Agreement is the blank 'Other provisions' referenced by 7.2.2 and 8.1.1; that displacement leaves those cost exceptions without an Article 14 referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Financially solvent, able to pay all debts as they mature and possessed of sufficient working capital' is a soft solvency standard applied not only to the Contractor but to 'the Subcontractors' generally, whom the Contractor may not yet have selected.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Subcontractors are selected later under Agreement 10.1 and Addendum 6.5 bidding, so a present warranty about all Subcontractors' solvency cannot be reconciled with the procurement sequence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Sufficient experience and competence' is a vague qualitative standard, though the list of items to be furnished is concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.4 and Addendum Article 2's skilled-staff requirement; no conflict.
judgments.clause_name: 14.6(b) Ability to furnish plant, tools and labor

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite and verifiable licensing warranty; 'quasi-public authorities' is a mild reach but conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 3.7 and the license number appearing on the Exhibits; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A site-visit and correlation warranty; 'familiar with the local conditions' is soft but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Mirrors A201 1.5.2 and 3.2.1, but the Contract Documents' Drawings and Specifications are 'TBD' at execution, so correlating observations 'with the requirements of the Contract Documents' is not yet possible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite identification of the Agreement as modified by the First Addendum; note it drops the 1997 edition qualifier present elsewhere but names the document.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cures the garbled edition reference in Agreement 15.1.1 and matches Article 1's precedence rule; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: A201 1997 Edition as modified by the Supplementary Conditions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Directly corrects Agreement 15.1.2's '1991 edition' reference; the correction is clear but the two statements coexist in the enumerated documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite incorporation of A201 Articles 1 through 14 with a naming convention; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 15.1.2 [Revision] and the Agreement's front-page note adopting A201 by reference; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: States that the supplements 'modify, change, delete from, and add to' and that unaltered provisions remain in effect; workable, though it never says how a supplement that neither cites nor tracks an A201 paragraph is to be integrated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Article 1's precedence rule and 1.2.1.1's better-quality/more-stringent rule, there are now three overlapping conflict-resolution mechanisms; that layering is the weak point.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad in reach ('wherever ... a matter requires notice to ... the Architect'), and internally in tension: it grants sweeping Owner approval rights while disclaiming any Owner responsibility for means, methods or safety 'notwithstanding any of the rights and authority granted the Owner.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It doubles every Architect consent under A201 (including 4.2.7 submittal review and 4.2.13 aesthetic decisions, which A201 makes final) with Owner consent, materially altering the Architect's decisional role under A201 4.2 and 4.4.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires the Contractor to provide 'the better quality or greater quantity' or comply with 'the more stringent requirement,' 'either or both' per the Architect's interpretation — the 'either or both' and the better/greater/more stringent tests are genuinely indeterminate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It directly competes with Agreement Article 1's rule that this Agreement governs inconsistencies, and with 15.1.1/15.1.2's precedence hierarchy; a court would have to choose between a hierarchy rule and a maximise-the-obligation rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise precedence rule between given dimensions and scaled measurements and between drawing scales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 1.1.5 and 1.2.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation of measurement risk with an absolute 'no extra charge' rule, followed by a duty to submit differences for resolution; the two sit slightly awkwardly but the rule is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Against A201 3.2.1's limited field-measurement duty and 4.3.4's concealed-conditions relief, the absolute no-extra-charge rule for dimensional differences narrows Contractor claims; broadly reconcilable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Minor change ... found necessary due to actual field conditions' overlaps with 'minor change' in A201 7.4 but is triggered differently; 'sufficiently detailed drawings' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 7.4.1 gives the Architect authority to order minor changes by written order, whereas here the Contractor submits drawings for Owner and Architect approval; and Supplementary 7.1.3.1 says changes to Sum or Time occur only by Change Order — the routes are not aligned.
judgments.clause_name: 1.2.1.1(c) Minor change due to field conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Says the representative 'is Mary Williamson' and then provides that any Owner action 'shall be taken, made or given by Paul H. Stephens, Elle M. Stephens or Mary Williamson' — the singular designation and the three-person list are internally inconsistent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 14.3 and Addendum 14.3 name 'Mr. or Mrs. Paul Stephens or Mary Williamson,' and A201 2.1.1 requires a single representative with express authority to bind; the three designations do not match.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single seven-day notice and self-help right, subject to Architect prior approval; 'reasonable cost' is ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes A201 2.4.1's second-notice-and-second-seven-day-period structure without saying so expressly, so a reader comparing the two versions must decide which notice regime applies; the Supplementary Conditions' 'unaltered provision remains in effect' rule makes that comparison necessary.
judgments.clause_name: 2.4.1 [Revision] Owner's right to carry out the Work

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite duties to monitor, advise and update, though 'shall be deemed attached to Document A111 as a part of the Contract Documents' as the schedule 'is developed' makes the document's content a moving target.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 15.1 enumeration (which lists no schedule) and with 3.10.5's phase-based revisions; making an evolving schedule a Contract Document creates uncertainty about what is binding when.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerates three phases and the deliverables, but 'Following completion of pre-construction services by Contractor' and the '75% Design Development Phase' are undefined terms in this instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cost estimates and the Schedule become Contract Documents, overlapping Addendum 6.5's Preliminary Budget and Schedule of Values; two parallel evolving pricing documents are not reconciled with 12.1.5's schedule of values or with Article 15's enumeration.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'All shop drawings necessary for any architectural, structural, mechanical or electrical work' plus a warranty of preparer 'expertise and experience' — the enumerated trades and the qualitative warranty are the soft points.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 3.12.10 limits the Contractor's obligation to provide professional design services and allocates design-criteria responsibility to Owner and Architect; this clause's warranty about licensed-engineer preparation edges into that allocation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and definite pleading requirements for time claims, with a documentation catch-all 'as the Owner may require.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 4.3.7.1 and 4.3.2's time limits; supplementary rather than contradictory.
judgments.clause_name: 4.3.7.3 [New] Claims for increase in Contract Time

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is garbled ('for each aie of the number of cause. of delay'), and 'concurrent or interrelated effects' is an open standard for apportioning delay.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sits against A201 8.3.1's entitlement to extension for enumerated causes; the no-separate-increase rule limits that entitlement in ways not fully spelled out.
judgments.clause_name: 4.3.7.4 [New] No separate increase for concurrent delays

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in its core rule (changes only by Change Order) but sweeping in its negation of course of conduct, implied acceptance and unjust enrichment, and its parenthetical 'whether or not there is, in fact, any unjust enrichment to the Work' reads oddly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excepts only A201 7.3 and 9.7.1, yet A201 7.4 minor changes, 4.3.4 concealed conditions, 8.3.1 extensions, 10.6.1 emergencies and Supplementary 1.2.1.1's better-quality rule can all alter Sum or Time without a Change Order; that is a genuine whole-instrument tension.
judgments.clause_name: Supplementary Conditions § 7.1.3.1 — Changes Only by Change Order

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A broad final-settlement clause enumerating direct and indirect costs, Fee and Schedule adjustments, closing with 'including, but not limited to' — the accord's scope is expansive but stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with 4.3.7.4's bar on separate time increases for concurrent delays and 7.1.3.1's Change-Order-only rule, this creates a tight waiver regime; consistent in direction with those clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Notwithstanding anything herein to the contrary' plus 'in their sole discretion' is a strong one-sided grant, and the pronoun 'their' for the Owner is a grammatical slip; the no-privity disclaimer is clearly drawn.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cuts across A201 9.6.2's requirement that the Contractor pay Subcontractors out of amounts received and 9.6.7's trust-like holding duty; joint payments alter that flow without addressing the interaction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: warranties assembled and delivered with the final Application, and no final Certificate until received and accepted by the Owner.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Adds an Owner-acceptance condition to the Architect's certification duty under A201 9.10.1 and Agreement 12.2.3's seven-day certification deadline; the Owner-acceptance gate can conflict with those fixed deadlines.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear exclusion keyed to whether the capital value is 'included in the Work,' with a waiver-of-subrogation requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 11.4.1.1 and 11.4.7, and with 7.5.1's treatment of tools not customarily owned; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite cost-shifting rule with an enumerated but illustrative parenthetical of recoverable costs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallels A201 11.4.1.2's Owner-failure rule and Addendum 7.7.3's insurance proviso, but Agreement Article 16's blank leaves 'insurance required under Article 11' partly undefined.
judgments.clause_name: 11.6 [New] Failure to purchase or maintain insurance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Says the hand-tool cost 'shall be borne by the Contractor' and then adds a flat 5% to payroll to cover those very tools, with an open list 'include, but are not limited to' — the borne-by-Contractor statement and the reimbursable markup pull in opposite directions in the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7.5.1 reimburses tools not customarily owned by workers at cost less salvage while 8.1.7 excludes anything not expressly described in Article 7; a percentage markup is neither, so this exhibit is hard to reconcile with Articles 7 and 8.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit C — Labor, Equipment and Hand Tools

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A specific 1% rate on 'total labor and subcontractors' costs' billed monthly; definite except that 'labor costs' is not tied to a defined Article 7 category.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7.6.1 reimburses only 'that portion of insurance ... directly attributable to this Contract' — an actual-allocation test — whereas this fixes a formulaic 1%; the two measures differ.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D — Commercial General Liability Insurance Premium Rate

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines 'Subcontract' costs and then extends the label to 'certain vendors' costs' with an open 'etc.' list; the ejusdem generis reach of that extension is uncertain, and 4.166% is a rate whose application to particular items is left to that list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 7.6.2 reimburses taxes 'related to the Work' without this exclusion structure, and 8.1.7 excludes unlisted costs; the exhibit's tax-base carve-outs must be squared with those.
judgments.clause_name: Exhibit D — State of Hawaii General Excise Tax Rate

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definitional list closing with an express statement of what the Contract Documents do not include; the enumeration of Modification types is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 1 says enumeration appears in 'Article 11' while it is in Article 15, and 15.1.3–15.1.5 leave Specifications and Drawings 'TBD'; the definitional structure assumes documents that were never enumerated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite integration clause with enumerated no-privity carve-outs and a stated Architect enforcement right.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 6.5, 3.10.4 and 3.10.5 make later-developed budgets, estimates and schedules part of the Contract Documents, which complicates 'entire and integrated agreement' and the Modification-only amendment rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The construction and services required by the Contract Documents' plus 'all other labor, materials, equipment and services provided or to be provided by the Contractor to fulfill the Contractor's obligations' is broad but structurally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With Drawings and Specifications 'TBD' in 15.1.4–15.1.5, the content of the Work is defined by reference to documents not yet enumerated; that gap is real.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with A201 6.1 and 1.1.3; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional, closing with 'generally including' an illustrative list; ordinary.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.5 lists no Drawings and dates them 'TBD,' so the definition operates on an empty set at execution.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.4's Specifications reference chains to a Project Manual dated 'none,' so the defined term has no identified content.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A volume assembled for the Work which may include' is permissive and vague about contents, but it is a definition of convenience.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 15.1.3 states the Project Manual is dated 'none' with contents 'TBD,' so no Project Manual exists to define; 15.1.4 depends on it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on 'reasonably inferable from them as being necessary to produce the indicated results' — a classic interpretive battleground — and on the complementarity rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read with Supplementary 1.2.1.1's better-quality/more-stringent rule and Agreement 5.2.6's 'reasonably inferable' language, three overlapping scope-inference rules operate at once.
judgments.clause_name: A201 1.2.1 Intent of the Contract Documents

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite disclaimer that Specification organisation does not control trade division.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.2.1 and with Agreement 10.1's subcontracting scheme; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Refers to words with 'well-known technical or construction industry meanings' used 'in accordance with such recognized meanings' — an invitation to extrinsic trade-usage evidence, which is inherently contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with the integration clause in 1.1.2, and with Exhibit C/D's trade terminology; consistent in structure though it opens the door to usage disputes.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A mechanical capitalization convention with three enumerated categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent throughout; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An anti-expressio-unius rule about omitted modifiers; it is definite in itself but expressly limits a standard canon of construction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.2.1's complementarity principle; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: documents shall be signed, and the Architect identifies unsigned ones on request.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Agreement, Addendum and Supplementary Conditions execution blocks have blank dates and some unsigned pages, so the identification mechanism matters here but no term contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed representation about site visit and correlation with Contract Document requirements; standard, though 'generally familiar' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum 14.6(d) warrants the same facts expressly, and the Drawings/Specifications were 'TBD' at execution, so the correlation representation has an uncertain object.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long, carefully drafted ownership and use provision with enumerated permissions and restrictions; the only softness is 'appropriate to and for use in the execution of their Work.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.2.5's furnishing of copies and 3.11.1's record set; no conflict identified.
judgments.clause_name: A201 1.6.1 Ownership and use of Drawings and Specifications

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite fifteen-day response with a specified content requirement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 4.1's Owner mortgage-filing blank is empty and A201 8.2.2 requires the Contractor to give notice before commencing for lien filing; the mechanisms coexist without contradiction.
judgments.clause_name: A201 2.1.2 Evidence of record legal title

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable evidence that financial arrangements have been made' is a vague sufficiency standard, and 'shall not materially vary such financial arrangements' without notice is likewise open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A201 14.1.1.4 makes failure to furnish this evidence a termination ground, so the vague standard has hard consequences; otherwise consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear division of responsibility with an express cross-reference to 3.7.1.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement 7.6.3 and A201 3.7.1; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite Owner obligation with a Contractor reliance right qualified by exercising 'proper precautions relating to the safe performance of the Work.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with 3.2.1's review duty and 4.3.4's concealed conditions; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Reasonable promptness' and 'any other information or services relevant to the Contractor's performance ... under the Owner's control' are both open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 3's Owner timeliness covenant and A201 14.1.4; no conflict, though the breadth of 'relevant' could be argued.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Such copies ... as are reasonably necessary' is a soft quantity standard, but the concept is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.6.1's ownership provisions and with 15.1.3–15.1.5's Project Manual references (which are TBD); minor dependency only.
judgments.clause_name: A201 2.2.5 Copies of Drawings and Project Manuals

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite stop-work right with an express disclaimer of any duty to exercise it 'except to the extent required by Subparagraph 6.1.3'; that cross-reference to coordination duties is an odd fit for a stop-work duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The cited 6.1.3 concerns coordination of separate contractors, which does not obviously create a stop-work duty; the cross-reference does not align with the rest.
judgments.clause_name: A201 2.3.1 Owner's right to stop the Work

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed two-notice, two-seven-day-period self-help mechanism with a clear cost-recovery rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary Conditions 2.4.1 [Revision] replaces this with a single seven-day notice, so two versions of the same numbered provision exist and 2.3.1 and 12.2.2 cross-refer to 'Paragraph 2.4.'
judgments.clause_name: A201 2.4.1 Owner's right to carry out the Work

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement's identification of Metzler Contracting and with Addendum Article 2's designated supervisory employee; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definite obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 2 and Addendum Article 2 [Revised]; no conflict.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.1.2 Contractor to perform the Work

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite non-relief rule enumerating the Architect's activities and third-party tests.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.2.2, 4.2.7 and 13.5; coherent.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.1.3 Contractor not relieved of obligations

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long provision that both imposes a study-and-compare duty and disclaims that the purpose is discovering errors, then requires prompt reporting of errors discovered — the disclaimer and the duty sit in tension within the same paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 1.2.1.1(b) makes the Contractor responsible for verifying measurements with no extra charge, which sharpens the tension with this clause's limited-purpose disclaimer.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.2.1 Review of Contract Documents and field conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Draws a line between review 'in the Contractor's capacity as a contractor and not as a licensed design professional' and a duty to report nonconformity 'discovered by or made known to' the Contractor; the boundary is workable but contested in practice.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 3.12.7.1's warranty about shop drawings prepared by licensed engineers and A201 3.12.10 bear on the same line; consistent in direction.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.2.2 Design errors or omissions noted

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite claim-routing plus a cost-shifting consequence for failure to perform 3.2.1/3.2.2 obligations, closing with a limited liability carve-out keyed to 'knowingly failed to report.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with 4.3.6, 4.3.7 and Supplementary 7.1.3.1's Change-Order-only rule; the claim routes are consistent.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.2.3 Additional cost or time from clarifications

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The excerpt turns on 'substitutions not properly approved,' 'may be considered defective,' and exclusions for 'improper or insufficient maintenance, improper operation, or normal wear and tear and normal usage' — several open-textured exclusions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interacts with 12.2.2's one-year correction period and Supplementary 9.10.1.1's warranty assembly; consistent in direction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Whether or not yet effective or merely scheduled to go into effect' is clear; the clause is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit D elaborates the excise-tax basis and exclusions, which supplements rather than contradicts, though its subcontract carve-out narrows the tax base.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite allocation with a temporal test ('customarily required after execution ... legally required when bids are received or negotiations concluded').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.2.2 and Agreement 7.6.3; also with Addendum 4.1's 'pending approval of permits.'

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definite compliance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.3, 3.7.4 and 10.2.2; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: no duty to ascertain, but a duty to notify on observation, with changes by Modification.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.2.2 and Supplementary 1.2.1.1's code-conflict rule requiring the more stringent requirement; the two together are workable.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.7.3 Not Contractor's responsibility to ascertain

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Knowing it to be contrary' is a scienter test and 'appropriate responsibility' is vague, but the cost allocation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.7.3 and 3.2.3; no conflict.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.7.4 Work performed contrary to laws

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite, subject to the soft 'reasonable objection' standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.4's allowance blank is empty, so this operates on nothing here; not a contradiction, merely inapplicable.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.8.1 Allowances included in Contract Sum

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully itemised allocation of what allowances cover and how Change Orders reflect differences; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Depends on allowances stated in the Agreement, and 5.2.4 is blank; otherwise consistent with 7.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In sufficient time to avoid delay' is soft but the obligation is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.3.1's delay causes and 3.10's schedule; no conflict.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.8.3 Selection of materials under allowance

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: competent superintendent, notice-binding effect, and confirmation of important communications in writing; 'important' is the one soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Addendum Article 2 requires 'one appropriately skilled and experienced supervisory employee' responsible for the project, and Agreement 14.4 names a project manager; whether these are the same role is unstated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite duty to submit and keep current a submittal schedule coordinated with the construction schedule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Supplementary 3.10.4/3.10.5 and 4.2.7; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'In general accordance with the most recent schedules submitted' is a loose performance standard, and 'submitted' rather than 'approved' leaves the binding document unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 3.10.4 deems the Construction Schedule a Contract Document as developed and 3.10.5 requires phase revisions, so which schedule governs at a given moment is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.10.3 Perform Work in accordance with schedules

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite record-keeping and delivery obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 1.6.1's record-set retention and Agreement Article 11's accounting records; coherent.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.11.1 Documents and samples at the site

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional; 'specially prepared for the Work' is the operative limit and is clear enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Supplementary 3.12.7.1's shop-drawing requirements; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional list closing with 'other information furnished by the Contractor to illustrate materials or equipment' — a mild catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.5 and 4.2.7; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short definitional provision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.11 and 4.2.7; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Draws the important line that submittals are not Contract Documents and that informational submittals may be identified; 'not expected to take responsive action' is soft.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 3.10.4/3.10.5 and Addendum 6.5 make certain later documents Contract Documents, so the categorical statement here needs qualification against them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: review, approve, submit with reasonable promptness and in sequence causing no delay; unmarked submittals may be returned without action.

judgments.clause_name: A201 3.12.5 Contractor to review and submit

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A deemed representation of determination, verification and coordination; clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.8 and Supplementary 1.2.1.1(b)'s measurement verification; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed but intricate: relief from deviations requires specific written notice at the time of submittal plus either written Architect approval of the deviation 'as a minor change' or a Change Order; workable though the conditions are layered.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 7.1.3.1 says changes to Sum or Time only by Change Order, which constrains the 'minor change' route here and in 7.4.1; the interaction requires care.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.12.8 Work in accordance with approved submittals

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite attention-directing duty with a stated consequence for silence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.12.8 and 4.2.7; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 3.12.7.1 warrants that shop drawings be prepared by expert persons and, where required, a licensed engineer, which pushes design responsibility toward the Contractor in tension with this clause's allocation and its condition precedent that all criteria be specified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall not unreasonably encumber the site' is a soft standard but the rule is conventional.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2.1's access obligations and 3.15's cleaning duties; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite responsibility statement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2.5's allocation to Owner and separate contractors; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite consent regime with mutual not-unreasonably-withheld qualifiers; 'endanger a portion of the Work' is broad but usable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 6.2 and 6.1.1's separate-contractor scheme; coherent.
judgments.clause_name: A201 3.14.2 Not to damage other construction

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Wherever located' and 'in preparation and progress' are broad but the access duty is plain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Agreement Article 11's audit access and 13.5's inspections; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite defence and hold-harmless with carve-outs for Owner/Architect-specified designs and Owner/Architect-prepared documents, plus a scienter-based exception; the exception's 'reason to believe' is the soft point.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 7.6.5 makes certain royalty and defence costs reimbursable and excludes others from Fee and GMP; the two must be read together, and the GMP is N/A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long, standard-form indemnity carefully limited to bodily injury and tangible property damage 'other than the Work itself' and to the extent caused by negligent acts; the opening reference to Project Management Protective Liability insurance not being purchased is the conditional element.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 11.3 was not exercised as far as the record shows, and Agreement Article 16's insurance blank leaves coverage undefined; the indemnity's 'to the extent claims are not covered by' trigger therefore has uncertain application.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear anti-limitation rule regarding workers' compensation and benefit acts.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 3.18.1 and 11.1.1.1; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional and clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Agreement's naming of Kerr/Howeson and 4.1.2/4.1.3; coherent.

judgments.clause_name: A201 4.1.2 Duties not restricted without consent

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite successor mechanism with a 'no reasonable objection' limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.1.2; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines the Architect's role and periods of representation clearly, ending with authority only as provided in the Contract Documents unless modified in writing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 1.1.2.1's blanket Owner-consent overlay and 1.2.1.1's 'Architect's interpretation as approved by the Owner' materially reshape this role; the two schemes must be reconciled.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.2.1 Architect's administration of the Contract

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite disclaimer of Architect responsibility for the Contractor's failures and for acts of Subcontractors.

judgments.clause_name: A201 4.2.3 Architect not responsible for Contractor's failure

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except as otherwise provided ... or when direct communications have been specifically authorized' plus 'shall endeavor to communicate ... through the Architect' is a soft channel rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definite certification duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.4.1, Agreement 12.1.3 and 12.2.3, though Agreement 12.1.3's own deadlines are garbled.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.2.5 Architect's certification of Applications for Payment

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 1.1.2.1 adds an Owner-consent layer to submittal review without adjusting timing, and 3.12.7 bars performing Work until approval; the added approver strains the promptness scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite grant of authority.

judgments.clause_name: A201 4.2.8 Change Orders and Construction Change Directives

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite duties regarding inspections, dates of Substantial Completion and final completion, and receipt of warranties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 9.10.1.1 conditions the final Certificate on Owner acceptance of warranties, and Addendum 12.2.1 adds recordation; the certification path is layered but reconcilable.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.2.9 Substantial Completion and final Certificate

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Conditional on Owner and Architect agreement, with duties 'as set forth in an exhibit to be incorporated in the Contract Documents' — no such exhibit exists here.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article 15's enumeration lists Exhibits A–E, none of which is a project-representative exhibit; the contemplated document is absent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in duty but the timing is expressed as 'within any time limits agreed upon or otherwise with reasonable promptness,' followed by a rule that no delay claim arises until 15 days after written request — the two timing standards coexist uneasily.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 1.1.2.1 requires Owner concurrence in Architect interpretations, which can delay responses beyond 'reasonable promptness'; the interaction is unaddressed.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.2.11 Architect's interpretations on written request

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Rests on interpretations being 'consistent with the intent of and reasonably inferable from' the Contract Documents and on immunity for decisions 'rendered in good faith'; both are open standards.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 1.2.1.1 makes the Architect's interpretation subject to Owner approval, which cuts against the neutral-interpreter premise and the no-partiality duty here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Aesthetic effect' is an undefined and notoriously elastic category, and making such decisions 'final' if 'consistent with the intent expressed in the Contract Documents' compounds the difficulty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Excluded from mediation and arbitration by 4.5.1 and 4.6.1, yet Supplementary 1.1.2.1 reserves aesthetic control to the Owner; whose aesthetic decision is final is unresolved.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines Claim broadly to include 'other disputes and matters in question ... arising out of or relating to the Contract,' a general catch-all appended to enumerated categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Interlocks with 4.4, 4.5, 4.6 and Agreement 12.2.4's direct arbitration right; the breadth of 'Claim' determines which route applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 21-day limit measured from the occurrence or from when the claimant 'first recognizes the condition,' 'whichever is later' — the recognition trigger is subjective but conventionally worded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 4.3.7.3 adds pleading detail and 4.3.4 has its own 21-day observance rule; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite duty to continue performing and paying pending resolution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 9.7.1's stop-work right as an express exception and Article 14; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Turns on conditions that 'differ materially' from those indicated or from those 'ordinarily found to exist and generally recognized as inherent in construction activities of the character provided for' — a heavily litigated standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Contract Documents' Drawings and Specifications are 'TBD,' so what was 'indicated in the Contract Documents' is uncertain; Supplementary 1.2.1.1(b) also bars extra charge for dimensional differences.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.3.4 Claims for concealed or unknown conditions

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An enumerated list of six reasons closed with 'or (7) other reasonable grounds' — a general catch-all against specifics, whose reach is precisely the ejusdem generis problem.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 7.1.3.1 bars increases except by Change Order, so claims on 'other reasonable grounds' must be squared with that restriction.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.3.6 Additional costs for stated reasons

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite notice requirement with content elements; 'only one Claim is necessary' for continuing delay is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supplementary 4.3.7.3 adds detailed content requirements and 4.3.7.4 restricts concurrent-delay increases; supplementary rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Abnormal for the period of time' and 'could not have been reasonably anticipated' are vague weather standards requiring extrinsic baselines.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 8.3.1's 'unusual delay in deliveries, unavoidable casualties' and Supplementary 4.3.7.3's documentation requirements; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Within a reasonable time not exceeding 21 days' pairs an elastic standard with a hard cap, and 'sufficient detail' is soft; still, the rule is intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.3.2 and 10.2.5; coherent.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.3.8 Injury or damage to person or property

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Materially changed' and 'substantial inequity' are both open-textured triggers for equitable adjustment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement 5.2.3 leaves unit prices blank, so this clause has no object here; not contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully drafted mutual waiver with enumerated categories and an express preservation of liquidated direct damages; the phrase 'liquidated direct damages, when applicable' is the only soft spot.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerates five permitted actions including advising that the Architect is 'unable to resolve' or that it 'would be inappropriate' in the Architect's 'sole discretion' — a broad discretionary escape from the decision duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive consultation right; definite in operation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and the Owner's accountants' role in Agreement 12.2.3; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite ten-day response window with three permitted responses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.4.2 and 4.4.5; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be read with 4.4.6's 30-day demand rule and Agreement 12.2.4's separate 30-day arbitration right on final accounting; the finality concept operates differently across them.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.4.5 Approval or rejection by written decision

judgments.clause_name: A201 4.4.6 Demand for arbitration within 30 days

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Permissive notice-to-surety provision, twice repeating 'may, but is not obligated to'; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Agreement Article 16's bond requirements are blank and no performance bond is evidenced, so 'the surety, if any' likely has no referent; not a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite permission to comply with statutory lien deadlines pending Claim resolution.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2.1.2, 9.10.2 and Addendum 12.1.4(b)/12.2.2's lien mechanics; coherent.
judgments.clause_name: A201 4.4.8 Claim relating to mechanic's lien

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is degraded in the middle ('or ... currently in effect'), but the mechanism — AAA Construction Industry Mediation Rules, filing with the other party and AAA, 60-day stay — is discernible.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: equal sharing, place of the Project unless mutually agreed, agreements enforceable as settlements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 13.1's governing law and 4.6's arbitration venue silence; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite in structure — arbitration after initial decision or 30 days, with aesthetic-effect and waived claims excluded — though 'Claims relating to aesthetic effect' inherits the vagueness of 4.2.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite procedural rules for demand and filing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.6.1 and Agreement 12.2.4's demand mechanics; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Combines specified limits, a 'reasonable time' standard, and a statute-of-limitations backstop determined under 13.7.1 — three overlapping time measures in one sentence.

judgments.clause_name: A201 4.6.3 Time limits on demand for arbitration

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long joinder-limitation clause turning on whose 'presence is required if complete relief is to be accorded' and on interests that are not 'insubstantial' — both indeterminate thresholds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4.5 and 4.6.1, and with the absence of separate contractors here; the standards are internal to this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard and definite enforcement provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite mutual objection rule, resting on 'reasonable' and 'timely.'

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 14.3.2 and Agreement 13.4; coherent.
